note: Drew ruling 19. Class 1/2/3 x colour is the card: Class 1 Blue is NOT Class 2 Blue, and BCP proves they are distinct by print run -- Blue is /150, /99, /50 and Red is /75, /50, /25 across Classes 1, 2, 3. 100 players x 3 classes x {Base, Black, Blue, Red, Gold} = 1,500 rows. Black is unnumbered (BCP gives odds 1:2, 1:6, 1:20 by class, not a run); Gold is one-of-one for all 300 base cards. The 500 existing flat-colour rows (Base/Black/Blue/Red/Gold with no class) are retired by the companion fold list: a colour alone is an ambiguous address that cannot say which of three print runs it is, and blank never means Class 1. The four stray 'Class 1 Blue' rows already in the catalog are the CORRECT vocabulary and are kept. PARALLEL VOCABULARY (2026-09-09): 'Class 1 Blue' is character-for-character the shape of a card line (a short word, a digit, a capitalised word -- cf. 'BD 154 Adley Rutschman'), so the ingest's card-line guard skipped the 1,200 colour rows and admitted only the 300 bare 'Class N' rows; prod carried exactly that split. The 15 names below are declared as rungs of THIS product so the guard exempts them by exact match. The guard itself is unchanged for every other product: 'Series 2 Mike Trout' still reads as a card line.
